notes: 0.6.44：清掉 0.6.43 留下的两处不一致。① `package.json` 里历史字段 `dsh.engines.dsh` 还是 ">=0.2.2-rc.2"，与顶层 `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.2-rc.5"` 不一致——0.2.2 的运行时只读顶层，但老读者若读历史字段会看到更松的下限，现已对齐。② README 中英各有一处把宿主端口写死成 10297，实际端口每次启动会变（本次重启后是 15045），现改成 `127.0.0.1:<端口>` 并注明以 `DSH_WEB_URL` 为准。审计套件补了 2 条断言：历史字段必须与顶层一致、README 不得再写死端口。功能代码无改动。 0.6.43：修正 0.6.42 的版本下限。0.6.42 声明 engines.dsh ">=0.2.3"，但实测两台事情：① 当前 DSH 运行时是 0.2.2-rc.5，而 DSH 在安装与 profile 启动时都会强制检查 engines.dsh（用声明 ">=99.0.0" 的假插件在临时 profile 上复现了 incompatible-version 拒绝），写成 0.2.3 会让这台机器重启后加载不了插件；② 准入接口 connection.requestRejection / connection.admit 在 0.2.2-rc.5 的源码里就已经存在。所以下限改为 ">=0.2.2-rc.5"：既能保证跑在带准入检查的运行时上，又不会把当前运行时挡在门外。准入代码本身与 0.6.42 相同。 0.6.42：把 13 条 HTTP 路由接进宿主准入 —— 每条 `/config-sync/*` 进处理器前先问 `ctx.connection.requestRejection(request)`（Host/Origin 围栏 + 浏览器会话鉴权，与 GUI 的 `/api` 同一套），宿主没有 `connection` 服务时才退回插件自己的 `originAllowed`。修的是实测问题：裸 curl（不带 Origin、无 Cookie）打 `/config-sync/status` 曾返回 200，能读配置摘要与仓库路径、能触发推送/还原；现在返回 401，拒绝体只有 `{ok:false,error}`。同时补 `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.3"`，并新增审计套件 `route-admission`（16 条断言，覆盖 403/401/放行/无 connection 四种情形 + 「每条注册都套准入」的结构断言）。 0.6.41：① 面板在 WebDAV 模式下不再把「分支 / HEAD」和「落后 / 领先」渲染成 `? @ ?` 与 `?`：仓库目录只是普通文件夹（没有 .git）时，这两行改成「WebDAV 模式：这个目录不是 git 仓库，没有分支」与「WebDAV 模式不比提交前后」，未提交数量照常显示；元信息行的 `branch @ head` 尾巴也只在真有分支时才追加，否则写传输方式。② 市场索引的图标从 1240×1696 的整屏长图换成 180×180 图标，并撤掉三张旧版截图。③ README 顶部加 npm / release / license / platform / 12 组 / 自检六枚徽章。 0.6.40：只修工具链，插件行为与 0.6.39：更名与文档。面板 / 侧栏 / 设置摘要行统一叫「配置备份与同步」（Config Backup & Sync），副标题改成「多端配置备份、同步与还原：本机 → 仓库 → 云端 → 另一台机器」；包描述改成多端备份/同步/还原口径，补 backup / restore / webdav / multi-device 关键词；退出后同步窗口标题一起改名，日志 banner（== DSH 配置同步 / x ==）不动——面板靠它解析结果。README 重写头部：定位段、四件事表（配置 / 备份 / 同步 / 还原）、流程线、目录锚点、发布状态压成一张表、已知限制单列，并修掉头部停在 0.6.14 的陈旧数字。
notesEn: 0.6.44: cleans up two inconsistencies left by 0.6.43. (1) The legacy `dsh.engines.dsh` field still said ">=0.2.2-rc.2" while the top-level `engines.dsh` said ">=0.2.2-rc.5" — the 0.2.2 runtime only reads the top-level field, but an older reader would have seen a looser floor, so the two now agree. (2) The Chinese and English READMEs each hard-coded port 10297, which changes on every start (15045 after the latest restart); they now use `127.0.0.1:<port>` and point at `DSH_WEB_URL`. The audit suite gains two assertions: the legacy field must match the top-level floor, and the READMEs must not hard-code the port. No functional code changed. 0.6.43: fixes the version floor shipped in 0.6.42. 0.6.42 declared engines.dsh ">=0.2.3", but two measurements say otherwise: (1) the running DSH runtime is 0.2.2-rc.5, and DSH enforces engines.dsh both at install and at profile startup — a fake plugin declaring ">=99.0.0" was refused with incompatible-version on a scratch profile, so ">=0.2.3" would stop this machine from loading the plugin after a restart; (2) the admission APIs (connection.requestRejection / connection.admit) already exist in 0.2.2-rc.5 sources. The floor is now ">=0.2.2-rc.5": it guarantees a runtime with the admission gate while remaining installable on the current one. The admission code itself is unchanged from 0.6.42. 0.6.42: all 13 HTTP routes now pass through the Host admission gate first — every /config-sync/* handler asks ctx.connection.requestRejection(request) (Host/Origin fence + browser-session authentication, the same gate the GUI /api channel uses) and only falls back to the plugin's own originAllowed when the Host offers no connection service. This fixes a measured hole: a bare curl (no Origin, no cookie) against /config-sync/status returned 200 and exposed config digests, repo paths and the pending list, and could trigger push/restore; it now answers 401 with a body containing only {ok:false,error}. package.json also declares engines.dsh ">=0.2.3", and a new audit suite route-admission (16 assertions) covers the 403/401/allowed/no-connection cases plus a structural assertion that every webServer.register handler is gated. 0.6.41: (1) In WebDAV mode the panel no longer renders Branch / HEAD and behind/ahead as `? @ ?` and `?` — when the repo folder is a plain directory without .git, those two rows now say "WebDAV mode: this folder is not a git repository" and "WebDAV mode: no commit comparison", with the uncommitted count still shown; the header `branch @ head` tail is only appended when a branch really exists, otherwise it names the transport. (2) The market index icon changed from a 1240x1696 full-page screenshot to the 180x180 icon, and three stale screenshots were retired. (3) Six badges added to the top of the README. 0.6.40: tooling only, plugin behaviour identical to 0.6.39. One assertion in tools/clientcheck.mjs matched an implementation detail (`missing ? null :`); after 0.6.36 merged the cloud-repo card with the WebDAV transport card the code shape changed while the behaviour did not, so the assertion went stale and turned the CI publish gate red. It now checks the actual gate (`(!wdConfigured && !gitConfigured) ? null :` cancel button plus the card title). 0.5.x is about making live push readable and honest: the CLIXML progress stream of PowerShell -EncodedCommand used to be written verbatim into the push log (4.95 MB / 5069 lines in one run); it is now reduced to message text (errors first, then Message/ToString), deduplicated across chunks, capped at 40 lines with an 8 MB safety limit, and lines duplicated on stdout and stderr are written once. The host contract is now written from the client app version — first push used to fall back to <AppRoot>\version, which is the Electron version (44.7.0 in practice) and poisoned the contract so the two machines could never match; legacy contracts are reported once and ignored on both the JS and PowerShell sides. Restore dispatches by snapshot kind (profile/plugin/session), files whose placeholders can be expanded are no longer skipped, Resolve-AppRoot no longer throws DriveNotFoundException for absent drives, WebDAV body reads have their own timeout, and mistyped CLI flags are reported. 0.5.5 makes the "no visible window ⇒ kill the client" path explicit: force-killing is only authorized when the plugin itself asked the client to quit (immediate push/pull, confirmed auto-pull, update, restore); passive waits now only wait and say why, so hiding the client to the tray no longer gets it killed. 0.5.6 fills in what the macOS/Linux Node engine was missing: push now runs git add/commit/push (it used to capture only, so the cloud never changed), pull now fetches and fast-forwards before applying, and the host contract gate applies to the engine too (major mismatch blocks unless -AllowVersionDrift). Restore is now interoperable: flat PowerShell snapshots and the engine profiles/<name> layout can be restored by either side. 0.5.7 fixes plugin updates failing forever when DSH was started from a PowerShell 7 session: the 5.1 child inherited PS7 PSModulePath, so Get-FileHash and Invoke-WebRequest were unavailable and the old code reported that as a corrupted package. Scripts now repair the module path, ship a .NET sha256 and an HttpWebRequest download fallback, and report the real reason when hashing is impossible; precondition failures also write the result file so the panel can show them. 0.5.8 applies the same module-path repair inside dsh-sync-common.ps1 (dot-sourced by push/pull/restore/backup), so Compress-Archive and Expand-Archive recover too; a regression test poisons PSModulePath with the PowerShell 7 module directory first and proves Get-FileHash fails before the fix and works after, together with Invoke-WebRequest and the archive cmdlets. 0.5.9 hardens the download fallback: Invoke-WebRequest can be discoverable yet throw at invocation in a mismatched module environment, so the code now try/catches and falls back to .NET; the full URL download to sha256 verify to install chain was exercised against a local HTTP server. 0.6.0 stops token downloads from failing with a bare 401 in a broken module environment: the HttpWebRequest fallback drops the Authorization header (verified), so it now explains the cause and the workaround; the public-URL download to sha256 to install chain is verified against a local HTTP server. 0.6.1 fixes a serious WebDAV bug: directory listing still derived its parse base from the configured directory name, so any WebDAV root with a path prefix (Nextcloud /remote.php/dav/files/<user>, Jiyanguo /dav, Alist /dav) returned hrefs that never matched. Subdirectories were never listed: every push re-uploaded everything and pull only saw root-level files. Directory and file listing now share one base taken from the real request path, with tolerance for reverse-proxy prefix rewrites. 0.6.3 removes two silent hazards in the CLI: push/pull now verify that the target directory is itself the repository root, otherwise git walks up and would operate on an outer repository (verified: it hit the user home dotfiles repo index lock); restore no longer treats a typo in -SnapshotKind as profile, and no longer accepts any empty directory as a flat snapshot (it used to create a useless backup and print "restored (0 files)" before failing). 0.6.4 adds two containment guards: WebDAV download paths come from server-supplied hrefs, so every segment is now validated (dot-dot, empty segment, absolute path, drive letter, NUL are refused and recorded, and the path is checked before any request is made); conflict restore now returns 400 when a list entry would write outside the repo. Testing showed the old code did not actually escape (a single dot-dot name only resolves to the parent directory), but refusal is now explicit instead of relying on EISDIR by accident. 0.6.5 fixes a config-destroying bug: saving any setting from the panel (even just toggling auto-push) went through handleSettings, which wrote only a whitelist of fields, so webdavUrl / webdavUser / webdavPass / webdavDir / syncMode were written back as empty strings and the WebDAV configuration was wiped, silently falling back to git. Settings are now written on top of the raw on-disk JSON so only submitted fields change (unknown fields are preserved too). WebDAV "Download now" into an empty folder is allowed again — a fresh machine is supposed to fill an empty folder, but it was rejected with "this folder does not look like a sync repo". 0.6.6 fixes custom sync folders being impossible to save on macOS or Linux. The old code converted every path to backslashes and validated it with Windows drive/UNC rules, so POSIX absolute paths (/Users/..., /srv/...) were treated as invalid and silently dropped — the panel reported success while nothing was stored. Validation now lives in normalizeSyncExtraPaths() in runtime/platform.mjs (separate rules for win32 / darwin / linux, unit-testable), and rejected paths are no longer dropped silently: the whole save is refused with a 400 that names them. 0.6.7 fixes sync-scope checkboxes having no effect in the JS engine. PowerShell capture.ps1 / apply.ps1 read config-sync-scope.json, but runtime/sync-engine.mjs never did (it only listed that file as "do not sync"). macOS and Linux have no PowerShell and run the engine, so groups unchecked in the panel — global prompts, skills, agent presets — were still captured and still restored, making the exclusions meaningless. The engine now applies the same rules (the required profile group is always on, plus group switches, per-item exclusions, and corrupt files treated as "everything enabled"), and both capture and apply report which groups were skipped. 0.6.8 fixes two ways the JS engine ignored custom roots (config-sync-roots.json). First, capture and apply only used detected dshHome / appRoot / workspaceHome with an always-empty custom map, so custom folder paths went into the repo as raw absolute paths and the other machine ended up pointing at the first machine folders; the user home folder was not normalized either, leaking the old username. Second, placeholder detection only matched ASCII names, so a custom root named in Chinese produced {{ROOT:...}} tokens that were neither recognized nor skipped, and the target machine wrote the literal token into its config. The engine now reads the roots file (same semantics as PowerShell Get-SyncRoots) and accepts any non-brace, non-space character in placeholder names. 0.6.9 fixes a corrupted conflict list being both invisible and impossible to clear. readConflicts treated "no file" and "broken file" as the same null, so GET reported exists:false (the panel said there were no conflicts) and POST rejected even action:reset before reaching it, leaving the user to delete the file by hand. The two cases are now distinguished: GET returns exists:true plus broken and error, other actions return 400 naming the corruption and suggesting a reset, reset is handled first and is idempotent, and the broken file itself is kept rather than overwritten. 0.6.10 fixes custom-root shape handling. In real files custom is an object map (PowerShell writes [ordered]@{}, the engine and panel both read and send that shape), but the save path only iterated the map: an array-shaped file (hand-edited, older, or copied from elsewhere) had each object stringified, so saving failed with "Custom folder must be an absolute path: 0 = [object Object]" — blocking the save and showing the user a meaningless message. All three shapes are now accepted (object map, [{name,path}], plain path array with the folder name as the key), each entry is still validated as an absolute path, and errors name the offending entry instead of printing [object Object]. 0.6.11 fixes machine paths leaking into the prompt files on Windows. Running capture.ps1 and apply.ps1 for real showed prompt/AGENTS.md was copied verbatim both ways (no tokenizing on capture, no expansion on apply), while the JS engine has always replaced the workspace path with {{WORKSPACE_HOME}} and expanded it on apply — and the panel says the repo stores placeholders. So an AGENTS.md pushed from machine A still named A's drive path after machine B pulled it. Both sides are now symmetric: capture replaces this machine's roots with placeholders before writing (still reporting "unchanged" when content matches) and apply expands them, warning and skipping instead of writing a literal {{...}} when a root on this machine is not confirmed yet. 0.6.12 (security): stop browser-profile leakage. Auditing the real repo on this machine found 3,696 files / 297.7 MB under plugin-data/browser-profiles/edge-cdp containing Login Data (the saved-password store), Cookies (session state), Web Data, Secure Preferences and History. The upload gate only matched a filename allowlist, .env, *.pem and GitHub token patterns, so none of these were caught and the next push would have shipped them to the cloud or a git remote. Three layers now block them: a path-segment denylist in the WebDAV gate, capture-side rejection plus a sweep that deletes previously captured copies from the repo (PowerShell), and the same list on the macOS/Linux engine; a 32 MB single-file cap was added too. 0.6.13: fixed interception wording. After the 32 MB single-file cap in 0.6.12, an oversized file was reported as a credential leak ("contains a token or local private credential"), which accuses the user of leaking secrets for what is only a size limit. Reasons are now distinct: secret (real credential), profile (browser profile data) and too-big (size limit, not a security issue, with a hint that such a file belongs in git mode). 0.6.14: closed the browser-profile gap in git mode. Previously only the WebDAV path was guarded, but in git mode `git add -A` stages every new file in the repo and commit history cannot be cleaned, so one wrong commit would leave Login Data and Cookies on the remote forever. The pre-commit gate now unstages profile paths using the same segment denylist, records them in .git/info/exclude and reports them separately as browser-profile/credential-store data. The pre-upload sweep for WebDAV honours the same list, and git mode was exercised end-to-end against a local bare remote for the first time (14 files really pushed). 0.6.15: fixed a hole where a user rules file disables the new safety defaults. This machine's ~/.dsh/config-sync-extra.json already carried an older snapshot (50 exclude patterns, 16 skipDirs without browser-profiles), and both fields are whole-list replacements, so the 0.6.12 defaults never applied: browser-profiles was still enumerated as an ordinary plugin slot (3,696 files / 297 MB on this machine) and only the hard per-file check stopped it, scanning all 297 MB for nothing. Safety-mandatory entries (skipDirs: browser-profiles; exclude: browser-profiles, User Data, Login Data, Cookies, Web Data, Local State) are now separated from the user-editable list, cannot be overridden, and are reported when added. 0.6.16: fixed machine-specific absolute paths inside profile yml/json being copied across machines verbatim. This machine's profile\cordis.patch.yml contains path: C:\Users\<user>\bin\pwsh7.cmd; capture copied those files byte-for-byte and restore wrote them back without expansion, so the path stayed wrong on the second machine (no such file, the tool cannot start). capture now rewrites root paths to {{APP_ROOT}} / {{DSH_HOME}} / {{WORKSPACE_HOME}} / {{ROOT:*}} before committing, and restore expands them for both git and snapshot modes, leaving non-path content byte-identical. A capture against the real ~/.dsh leaves zero raw C:\Users lines and two placeholder lines in cordis.patch.yml. 0.6.17: fixed local plugin links under the user home in profile/package.json. This machine has "@local/dsh-personal": "link:C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/dsh-personal"; capture only rewrote appRoot links, so it went into the repo verbatim, and apply only rewrote the built-in plugin names. On another machine pnpm install then resolved a path that does not exist and the profile failed to install. package.json now goes through the full tokenizer (userHome is already a root) and apply expands before writing. Verified against real data: the repo now carries link:{{ROOT:userHome}}/AppData/Local/dsh-personal, and a restore run with a fake USERPROFILE expands it to C:/Users/AuditOtherUser/... 0.6.18: fixed restoring with the sync repo as the snapshot, which is the path you take after a crash when no local backup exists. Real config plus a fake user name exposed three defects: (1) {{ROOT:userHome}} / {{DSH_HOME}} inside settings\dsh-workspaces.json were copied byte-for-byte into ~/.dsh, so DSH read literal placeholders as paths; (2) that file was also dropped at the ~/.dsh root while DSH actually reads ~/.dsh\storages\workspace.json, so the file came back but every workspace disappeared; (3) prompt\AGENTS.md exists in the repo but restore only looked for a flat AGENTS.md, so no prompt was restored at all. The settings map now lives once in dsh-sync-common.ps1 (shared by capture, apply and restore), restore places files by that map and expands placeholders, and HomeFiles falls back to prompt\. Also fixed my own use of [IO.Path]::GetRelativePath, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not have (it is .NET Core only) and which threw on a real machine. 0.6.19: closed the placeholders apply never expanded. Applying the real repo onto an empty machine left path: {{ROOT:userHome}}/bin/pwsh7.cmd inside profile\cordis.patch.yml and leftovers in pnpm-lock.yaml, because apply only expanded {{APP_ROOT}} / {{WORKSPACE_HOME}} and its post-write guard checked just those two tokens, so {{DSH_HOME}} / {{ROOT:*}} reached the local machine. The host parses that YAML as a string, but the tool path is a literal placeholder and the tool cannot start; lockfile specifiers also no longer match package.json. Expansion is now one step (AppRoot legacy fallback, then the whole token table) and the guard fails on any remaining {{. Re-verified with the real payload: 73 files applied, zero placeholders left. 0.6.20: concurrency guard and tolerance for broken configs. Two captures against the same DSH home collided on file locks and one threw a .NET stack trace (measured: WriteAllText "The process cannot access the file ... profile/package.json because it is being used by another process") — the real trigger is the auto watcher running while the user presses push in the panel. capture and apply now take a named Mutex (Local\, released automatically on process exit, so a crash cannot leave a deadlock); when it is held they print "another sync action is already running (same DSH home), this capture did not run" and exit 3 instead of pretending success. Also tested broken configs: a malformed config-sync-extra.json falls back to defaults, warns, and leaves the user file untouched; a broken dsh-config-sync.json no longer makes status crash or dump a stack trace. 0.6.21: wired exit code 3 into the panel. 0.6.20 made a mutex-blocked run return 3, but the panel treated any non-zero exit as failure: it turned red and picked an arbitrary line from the log tail as the reason (measured: it picked "then run (either one)"), so the user saw a push failure plus an unrelated hint. Code 3 now takes its own branch: message "Skipped: another sync is already running (not a failure)", recorded as finished with a skipped flag, and no more guessing from the tail. Static assertions guard both points (code 3 must call finish(true,…,{skipped:true}) and must have its own message). 0.6.22: exit code 3 used to trigger the automatic rollback in the background runner — found while following 0.6.21 through. post-exit.ps1 decided success with $failed = ($code -ne 0), so a 3 counted as failure and the pull branch ran its "rollback on failure": git reset --hard to the pre-pull commit plus restoring config from a snapshot. In other words, one collision between the auto watcher and a manual sync would reset a healthy repository. Now $skipped = ($code -eq 3) and $failed excludes it; the result text reads "another sync action is already running, this pull/push was skipped (not a failure)" instead of claiming a push failure. 0.6.23: exit code 3 was flattened to 1 by sync.ps1. Its push branch called Die on any non-zero from capture (Die always exits 1), so "another sync is running" became an ordinary failure one layer up; and PowerShell pipelines swallow a child script exit code (measured: post-exit saw 1). The chain needed two patches: sync.ps1 now exits 3 as-is (both webdav and git branches), and post-exit also recognises the "another sync action is already running" line in the output as a fallback. Verified by a real run: sync.ps1 push exits 3 while the mutex is held, prints both skip lines, and HEAD stays unchanged. 0.6.24: also tested the panel wrapper path the way it is really written. On Windows the live push does not call sync.ps1 directly; it wraps it in -EncodedCommand with $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' and a try/catch whose catch exits 1 — that layer could easily swallow 3 into 1. Measured: the wrapper passes 3 through, does not take the catch branch, and both skip lines are present, so no code change was needed; a fixture now guards it. Also documented a known gap in the README: on non-Windows the panel live push runs sync-engine.mjs (a pure Node capture/apply) with no mutex — concurrency protection today covers only the PowerShell side, and I have not run it on macOS/Linux, so it must not be claimed safe there. 0.6.24: also tested the panel wrapper path the way it is really written.
